newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - News paper fined for misleading ads.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - News paper fined for misleading ads.

text.p: News Corp Ltd's Daily Telegraph newspaper in Sydney has been fined A$120,000 for misleading the public over a 'free' mobile phone promotion, said competition regulator the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission.

The ACCC said News Corp unit Nationwide News Pty Ltd, publisher of Sydney's Daily Telegraph, was found guilty of six charges of misleading the public as to the effect of the conditions applying to the mobile telephone offer.
The advertisments in the then-Telegraph Mirror promised a 'free' mobile phone but the conditions attached to the offer, meant readers had to pay more than A$2,000 in charges, it said.
"The decision underlines the seriousness of misleading the public with this type of promotion," ACCC chairman Allan Fels said in a statement.
"Individual consumers may have purchased the paper only because of the promotion, then found it was not as good as deal as they expected," Fels said.
"This case shows that it is not enough to put an asterisk or'conditions apply' at the bottom of the advertisement when those conditions contradict the basic thrust of the advertisement," he said.
